title: haas job.json, version 1
description: The spec at the root of a job directory. It carries a brief, not a prompt. A reader fills in ref, sensitivity and budget when they are left out, and ignores a field it does not know. `haas new` writes every field except model, which it leaves out when empty.

version.description: The format of this file. A file without it is version 1. A reader refuses a version newer than it knows.

brief.description: What to do, in a person's words. It is input to the harness, which the adapter places in the harness's command line.

repo.description: The repository to work in: anything `git clone` accepts, a URL or a local path. The runner clones it into workspace/.

ref.description: What `git checkout` is given after the clone. A reader takes HEAD when it is empty or left out.

gate.description: The command that says pass or fail, as the program and its arguments. It runs in workspace/ with no shell, and the job passes when it exits zero. A job with an empty gate is refused when it runs.

harness.description: The name of the adapter that runs the work, looked for in harnesses/ inside the job directory, then in the directory HAAS_HARNESSES names, then among the built-in ones.

model.description: The model to ask for, put in place of {model} in the adapter. When empty or left out, the harness uses whatever it is configured with.

sensitivity.description: How sensitive the code is. Restricted code only talks to a model on this machine or a private network, and the runner refuses the job otherwise. A reader takes internal when it is empty or left out, and refuses any other label.

budget.description: What a job may spend before a runner stops it. A zero or missing member takes its default.

turns.description: The turns a harness may take. It is kept with the job; no runner enforces it yet, so the seconds are what stop a run.

seconds.description: The wall-clock seconds the harness may run. When they are spent the harness is killed and the manifest records stoppedAtBudget; the gate still runs.
